title: Accountant Salary Australia: Converting Hourly Rates to Annual Pay
description: Learn how to convert an hourly rate to annual salary for accountant salary Australia. Includes tax, super, casual loading, and Fair Work Ombudsman award rates.
salarySummary: For a full-time accountant on 38 hours per week, annual gross pay is hourly rate × 38 × 52, with super paid on top and tax deducted according to the 2026–27 resident scale.

faqs.q: How do I convert an hourly rate to an annual salary in Australia?
faqs.a: Multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a standard full-time role, use 38 hours per week. For example, $40 per hour × 38 hours × 52 weeks = $79,040 per year. This assumes the same rate every week with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. Use [the timesheet](/) to calculate your own figures.

faqs.q: What is the difference between the National Minimum Wage and award rates for accountants?
faqs.a: The National Minimum Wage from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour (or $33.05 for casuals including 25% loading). However, most accountants are covered by an award such as the Clerks – Private Sector Award or the Professional Employees Award, which set higher minimum rates. Always check the relevant pay guide from the Fair Work Ombudsman at [pay guides](/blog) to find the correct classification and rate for your role.

faqs.q: How is superannuation calculated on top of an accountant's salary?
faqs.a: Superannuation is paid on top of your ordinary earnings at the current rate of 12%, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. For example, if your annual salary is $80,000, your employer must contribute an additional $9,600 into your super fund. This is not deducted from your pay. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more details.

bodyMarkdown:
## Understanding Accountant Salary Australia

When researching **accountant salary Australia**, the first step is to understand how hourly rates translate into annual earnings. Whether you are a graduate, a senior accountant, or a contractor, the same basic formula applies: multiply your hourly rate by the hours you work each week, then multiply by 52 weeks. For a full-time employee, the standard week is 38 hours. This article explains the calculation, distinguishes between minimum wage and award rates, and covers tax and superannuation.

### The Hourly-to-Annual Formula

The core formula is:

**Annual gross pay = hourly rate × hours per week × 52**

For a full-time accountant working 38 hours per week, the calculation becomes:

Annual gross = hourly rate × 38 × 52

For example, an hourly rate of $45 gives $45 × 38 × 52 = $88,920 per year. This is the gross amount before tax and before super (which is paid on top). The same formula works for part-time roles if you use your actual weekly hours. If you are paid a salary, you can reverse the calculation to find your equivalent hourly rate: divide your annual salary by 52, then divide by your weekly hours.

### Fortnightly Pay

Many Australian employers pay fortnightly. To find your gross fortnightly pay, multiply your weekly pay by 2. Using the example above, weekly pay is $45 × 38 = $1,710, so fortnightly gross is $3,420. This can help you budget and compare with job advertisements that quote fortnightly figures.

### National Minimum Wage vs. Award Rates

The Fair Work Ombudsman sets the National Minimum Wage, which from 1 July 2026 is $26.44 per hour for employees aged 21 and over. Casual employees receive a 25% loading, making the minimum casual rate $33.05 per hour. However, most accountants are covered by an award – such as the Clerks – Private Sector Award or the Professional Employees Award – which provides higher minimum pay rates based on classification and experience. Always check the relevant pay guide on the Fair Work Ombudsman's website to ensure you are being paid correctly. You can also use the [pay guides](/blog) page to find the latest award rates.

### Casual Loading

If you work as a casual accountant, your hourly rate should include a 25% loading in lieu of paid leave. When using [the timesheet](/) calculator, type your base hourly rate (without loading) and tick the casual loading checkbox. The tool will add 25% on top. Do not enter a rate that already includes casual loading.

### Superannuation: Paid on Top

Superannuation is an additional contribution your employer must make to your super fund. The current rate is 12% of your ordinary earnings, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. Super is paid on top of your gross salary – it is not deducted from your pay. For an accountant earning $90,000 per year, the employer contributes an extra $10,800. This is separate from your take-home pay. See [super and packaging](/topics/super-and-packaging) for more information.

### Tax and Medicare Levy

Your annual gross pay is subject to income tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on the first $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

In addition, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The tax-free threshold is included in the above rates. For example, an accountant with a gross annual salary of $80,000 would pay approximately $16,267 in tax plus $1,600 in Medicare levy, leaving a take-home pay of about $62,133. Use the [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) page to estimate your net income.

### Benchmarking Accountant Salaries

While award rates set a floor, actual accountant salaries vary widely by experience, location, and industry. The Australian Bureau of Statistics (ABS) reports that full-time adult average weekly ordinary time earnings were $2,083.70 per week in May 2026, which equates to about $108,352 per year for a 38-hour week. This figure can serve as a rough benchmark for experienced accountants. However, graduate and junior roles often start closer to award rates, while senior accountants and managers may earn significantly more. Always compare offers against industry surveys and the relevant award.

### Important Assumptions

The calculations on this page assume:
- The same hourly rate applies every week (no unpaid overtime)
- No penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice
- Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base
- Tax uses the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold
- Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds (the 2026–27 thresholds were not confirmed at the time of this reference)

These are estimates, not a determination of your actual pay or tax liability. For personalised advice, consult a tax professional or use the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay and Conditions Tool.
